headline: Advancing Quantum Protocols, Simulation, and Measurement
summary: Today's research highlights major theoretical and algorithmic strides in quantum information science. The work spans secure blind quantum computation, foundational quantum measurement incompatibility, and efficient simulation of complex classical systems.

themes.title: Blind Quantum Computation
themes.body: A novel protocol enables low-resource clients to securely delegate computations to a server whose size scales only with the non-Clifford gate count.

themes.title: Quantum Measurements and Incompatibility
themes.body: Introduction of k-fold unbiased measurements extends projective measurement frameworks, leveraging Clifford algebras to analyze operational incompatibility.

themes.title: Quantum Simulation of Dissipation
themes.body: New quantum algorithms simulate classical oscillator networks with non-Markovian dissipation, achieving quartic speedups for locally coupled 3D systems.

connections.body: Both protocol design for blind quantum computation and the construction of k-fold unbiased measurements rely heavily on Clifford algebra structures.
